description: Solo team of Noamane Ouldelabbar, 5th-year Engineering Student in Big Data & AI at Ecole Polytechnique d'Agadir, Agadir, Morocco. Working on 'Be An Earth System Trend Detective!' — building Agadir Earth Trend Detective, a trend detector for summer temperatures in Agadir using NASA POWER data.
summary: Trend detector for summer temperatures in Agadir, Morocco (1981–2025) using NASA POWER data: Theil-Sen +0.25 °C per decade, Mann-Kendall p=0.041, a significant warming trend. Interactive time-series visualisation built with Python, FastAPI and React.
details: Problem: Morocco's summers are warming — but by how much, where, and is the change statistically significant? Our tool answers exactly that. Data: NASA POWER monthly 2-metre air temperature (T2M, MERRA-2 reanalysis), 1981–2025, for three Moroccan cities — Agadir (30.42°N, 9.60°W), Casablanca (33.57°N, 7.59°W) and Marrakech (31.63°N, 8.00°W). For each city we computed the June–July–August mean for all 45 summers. Method: Theil-Sen slope estimator for the trend magnitude and the Mann-Kendall test (5% significance level) to decide whether the trend is significant, plus decade means (1981–1990 vs 2016–2025) and hottest/coldest summers. Results: all three cities warmed significantly. Agadir: +0.25 °C/decade (p=0.041), 27.58 °C → 28.42 °C (+0.84 °C); hottest summer 2012 (30.37 °C), coldest 1997 (25.38 °C). Casablanca (oceanic, slowest): +0.18 °C/decade (p=0.046), 23.20 → 23.53 °C; hottest 2023 (24.91 °C). Marrakech (fastest): +0.45 °C/decade (p=0.002), 26.38 → 27.88 °C (+1.49 °C); hottest 2025 (29.59 °C). Tool: interactive web app — pick a city, see the 45-year series with its Theil-Sen trend line and decade means, compare the three cities, download the CSV. Data processing and statistics in Python; demo as an interactive web app. Limitations: POWER T2M is MERRA-2 reanalysis, not ground-station measurements; three cities and summer means only — the same method extends to any NASA variable, region and season. Sources: NASA POWER (power.larc.nasa.gov). AI assistance: AI tools (Muse) were used for coding/debugging the web app and for writing/editing this description. The statistical analysis used standard methods (Theil-Sen, Mann-Kendall, Python/scipy) on real NASA POWER data; no data was invented or generated.
